caseno: Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 7753, 7754 and 7755 of 2000
parties:
Monzur Alam (Md) ------ Petitioner
Vs.
State and another ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
4. We have perused the petitions of complaint of all three cases and the plaint of Title suit filed by the accused petitioner. In the petition of complaint we find that these were filed in respect of cheques issued by the accused petitioner in favour of the complainant. The cheques were dishonoured and thereafter observing the formalities of sending notice, etc. the complainant filed the petition of complaint under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act. Then the accused petitioner failed to make the payment. From the certified copy of the plaint we find that the accused petitioner alleged that there was an understanding between the parties who were directors of the said company and on the basis of this understanding and agreement, the petitioner agreed to make payment by cheques and already made payment of Taka 28, 42,955 but the plaintiff claimed that he suffered huge loss in the business and thereafter, the agreement became unenforceable. The defendant No. 3 also terminated and cancelled the agreement. So, the plaintiff prayed for a decree for a declaration that the deed of agreement and Memorandum of Understanding are void, inoperative and not binding upon him. We are of the view that the relief sought for in the suit has no connection with the offence as alleged in the petition of complaint filed by the complainant. The question to be decided in the three criminal cases is whether the cheques were issued by the accused, whether those were presented within time for encashment and dishonoured and whether notice was served according to law after getting the information of dishonouring of the cheques. In this criminal case there is no scope of making any inquiry as to the circumstances under which agreement was entered into between the parties or whether that agreement or understanding is legal or not. 

 5. On the other hand, if the understanding is not binding upon the accused petitioner and if he gets a decree in a Civil suit that will not absolve him of the liability of issuing cheques which were dishonoured. So, we find that there is no reason to stay the present cases filed under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments (Amendment) Act, 1994 due to the fact that the accused petitioner filed a Title suit challenging the agreement entered into between the parties, under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, an offence is committed if a cheque is dishonoured and if payment is not made within 15 days after receipt of a legal notice. So, if an offence is committed under the above section, the criminal Court will be competent to try the case and pendency of civil suit will not be in any way any hindrance to proceed with the criminal cases because there is no possibility of any conflicting decision in the civil suit and criminal cases. So, we find no substance in these Rules.
